Master Mobile Plan (2026) > Trigger device logs (coverage_matrix.csv XLSX Tab 'Trigger device logs') > 'Device Logs 1' - 'Set feature flag + install/login/submit/logout'. INTENTIONALLY NOT WIRED INTO hq_client.py's action dispatch - this is a ONE-TIME environment-setup step, not a per-run test pre-step, and it is a fundamentally different kind of HQ action than everything else in hq_client.py.

Why this is different from every other hq_setup/*.json in this repo: the other files here call app-management endpoints scoped to a single domain/app (release_build, save_copy, edit_commcare_profile, update_prompts) that are safe and expected to be re-run before every test run. This row instead describes toggling a Django *feature flag* (a superuser-only, typically Django-Admin-driven, toggle - see corehq/apps/toggles.py / corehq/apps/toggle_ui in the commcare-hq source, which hq_client.py has no client for) that (a) requires superuser/staff permissions beyond a normal domain-admin session, (b) is enabled per-domain or per-user ONCE and then left on indefinitely (it controls whether the mobile app's request/response device logs get surfaced at all), and (c) is exactly the kind of raw Django-Admin action coverage_matrix.csv already marks 'Not automatable' for this same tab's sibling row 'Device Logs 2' ('Django Admin - add domain/username... Django Admin is a raw desktop-browser admin page'). Scripting a one-time environment toggle into a per-test-run pre-step would be misleading - it would look like something CI re-applies every run, when in reality re-toggling it every run is unnecessary (and touches superuser-only surface area this framework's HQClient.login() isn't provisioned for). Treat this as a manual, once-per-QA-environment checklist item, not a `python scripts/hq_client.py ...` pre-step: log into the target domain as a superuser, enable the relevant feature flag via Django Admin (django_settings > toggle editor at /hq/flags/edit/<flag_slug>/, per corehq/apps/toggle_ui), and confirm it stays on across test runs.

The on-device half of this row ('install/login/submit/logout') needs no new or near-duplicate flow: it's exactly the composition of flows/common/login.yaml -> flows/common/submit_only_form.yaml (or an equivalent form-submit subflow already used elsewhere, e.g. by flows/updates_2_49/rate_limit_02_04_popup_dont_show_toast.yaml) -> flows/common/logout.yaml, run against whatever app/domain had the feature flag enabled per the manual step above. Writing a fourth flow that just chains those three existing subflows together would add no coverage beyond what those already prove individually, so none was added.
